BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN) — At least 59 people were killed and more than 200 others injured early Thursday when a fire broke out at an upscale Bangkok nightclub where approximately 1,000 revelers had gathered to usher in the new year, Thai police reported.

Rescue officials surveyed the scene of the devastating nightclub fire in Bangkok, Thailand. The majority of the victims perished from smoke inhalation or were trampled in the frantic rush to escape the venue. Thus far, thirty bodies have been identified—29 Thai nationals and one Singaporean, according to police.

The blaze erupted at the Santika nightclub at approximately 12:35 a.m., authorities stated. Rescue officials confirmed that 226 others were injured, among them several foreigners. Two Americans sustained injuries in the fire, a U.S. State Department official disclosed. While the official declined to release the victims' names or the severity of their injuries, he confirmed that the department remained in contact with them.

Steven Hall, a British national who was hurt in the blaze, told CNN that flames began to spread across the ceiling above the stage, where a band and DJ were performing. Alarmingly, some patrons appeared to believe the fire was part of the show. "At the same time there were people rushing to get out, there were other people who seemed to be lacking a sense of urgency and didn't seem to realize what was going on," Hall recounted.

The fire originated near a stage where fireworks were being deployed as part of a performance on the club's closing night, said police Maj. Gen. Chokchai Deeprasertwit.

"It may have been caused from sparks, but we don't know if it was sparks from guests or from the nightclub's countdown display on the nightclub stage," he explained.

Hall said his wife managed to escape ahead of him, but he became caught in the crowd. "The lights went out, and at that moment, my back started burning, and I was breathing in hot air," he recalled.

British citizen Andrew Jones said he had been celebrating in the area when he came upon the fire. He described seeing victims being rushed out on stretchers and spoke with witnesses, including a fellow Briton who had seen fireworks being lit onstage. "He immediately ran out of the building, but immediately when he'd done that, the lights went out, and he couldn't see," Jones said.

The club is situated in one of Bangkok's busiest commercial districts. Its website features images of bands and DJs performing on both indoor and outdoor stages, and boasts that it "innovatively blends the comfort of nature with the excitement of the Bangkok nightlife." The site had advertised the club's New Year's celebration, aptly named "Goodbye Santika."

CNN's Kocha Olarn contributed to this report.
